claims.sentence: The IRS puts the starting point plainly: when beginning a business, you must decide what form of business entity to establish, and the form you choose determines which income tax return you file.
claims.quote: you must decide what form of business entity to establish

claims.sentence: It lists the sole proprietorship, the partnership, the corporation and the S corporation as the most common forms, and it describes the limited liability company as a business structure allowed by state statute.
claims.quote: The most common forms of business are the sole proprietorship, partnership, corporation, and S corporation

claims.sentence: It lists the sole proprietorship, the partnership, the corporation and the S corporation as the most common forms, and it describes the limited liability company as a business structure allowed by state statute.
claims.quote: A limited liability company (LLC) is a business structure allowed by state statute

claims.sentence: The IRS says each state may use different regulations for limited liability companies, and that owners are called members.
claims.quote: Each state may use different regulations

claims.sentence: The IRS says each state may use different regulations for limited liability companies, and that owners are called members.
claims.quote: Owners of an LLC are called members

claims.sentence: Most states do not restrict who may be a member, so members can be individuals, corporations, other LLCs or foreign entities, and there is no maximum number.
claims.quote: Most states do not restrict ownership, so members may include individuals, corporations, other LLCs and foreign entities

claims.sentence: Most states also permit an LLC with a single owner.
claims.quote: Most states also permit "single-member" LLCs, those having only one owner

claims.sentence: A domestic LLC with at least two members is classified as a partnership unless it files Form 8832 and elects to be treated as a corporation.
claims.quote: a domestic LLC with at least two members is classified as a partnership for federal income tax purposes unless it files Form 8832

claims.sentence: An LLC with one member is treated as an entity disregarded as separate from its owner for income tax, unless it makes the same election.
claims.quote: an LLC with only one member is treated as an entity disregarded as separate from its owner

claims.sentence: The IRS adds that for employment tax and certain excise taxes, a single-member LLC is still considered a separate entity.
claims.quote: for purposes of employment tax and certain excise taxes, an LLC with only one member is still considered a separate entity

claims.sentence: Delaware's LLC statute states a policy of giving the maximum effect to the principle of freedom of contract and to the enforceability of limited liability company agreements.
claims.quote: give the maximum effect to the principle of freedom of contract and to the enforceability of limited liability company agreements

claims.sentence: The IRS describes forming a corporation as prospective shareholders exchanging money, property or both for the corporation's capital stock.
claims.quote: prospective shareholders exchange money, property, or both, for the corporation's capital stock

claims.sentence: For federal income tax purposes, a C corporation is a separate taxpaying entity.
claims.quote: a C corporation is recognized as a separate taxpaying entity

claims.sentence: The IRS explains that its profit is taxed to the corporation when earned and taxed again to shareholders when distributed as dividends, which it calls a double tax.
claims.quote: taxed to the corporation when earned, and then is taxed to the shareholders when distributed as dividends

claims.sentence: The IRS explains that its profit is taxed to the corporation when earned and taxed again to shareholders when distributed as dividends, which it calls a double tax.
claims.quote: This creates a double tax

claims.sentence: It also notes that shareholders cannot deduct a loss of the corporation.
claims.quote: Shareholders cannot deduct any loss of the corporation

claims.sentence: In Delaware, the business and affairs of a corporation are managed by or under the direction of a board of directors.
claims.quote: managed by or under the direction of a board of directors

claims.sentence: In Delaware, the business and affairs of a corporation are managed by the board, except as the statute or the certificate of incorporation provides otherwise.
claims.quote: except as may be otherwise provided in this chapter or in its certificate of incorporation

claims.sentence: Its Division of Corporations describes certificate of incorporation and certificate of formation forms with instructions and fees.
claims.locator: How to form a new business entity, Certificate of incorporation / formation forms
claims.quote: Sample forms with instructions and fees are available

claims.sentence: Its Division of Corporations describes a name reservation that holds an entity name for 120 days.
claims.locator: How to form a new business entity, name reservation
claims.quote: will guarantee that your name is held for you for a period of 120 days

claims.sentence: Delaware's corporation statute provides that the consideration for stock is paid in the form and manner the board of directors determines.
claims.quote: shall be paid in the form and in the manner that the board of directors shall determine

claims.sentence: It allows stock to be issued for cash, for any tangible or intangible property, or for any benefit to the corporation.
claims.quote: consideration consisting of cash, any tangible or intangible property or any benefit to the corporation

claims.sentence: It allows stock to be issued in the numbers and at the times set by a resolution of the board.
claims.quote: in the numbers, at the times and for the consideration as set forth in a resolution of the board of directors

claims.sentence: Under the Internal Revenue Code, a person's rights in property are subject to a substantial risk of forfeiture if the person's rights to full enjoyment of the property are conditioned upon the future performance of substantial services by any individual.
claims.quote: rights to full enjoyment of such property are conditioned upon the future performance of substantial services by any individual

claims.sentence: The IRS describes property as substantially vested once it is transferable or is no longer subject to a substantial risk of forfeiture.
claims.quote: Property is substantially vested when: It's transferable, or It isn't subject to a substantial risk of forfeiture

claims.sentence: An employer sells an employee shares, and the employee must resell the stock to the corporation at the price paid if the employee leaves the job for any reason within a set period.
claims.quote: you must resell the stock to the corporation at $100 a share if you leave your job for any reason

claims.sentence: Because the person must perform substantial services over time, or give the stock back, the IRS treats the rights as subject to a substantial risk of forfeiture.
claims.quote: your rights to the stock are subject to a substantial risk of forfeiture

claims.sentence: Delaware's statute on restrictions on transfer says a written restriction on the transfer of a company's securities may be imposed by the certificate of incorporation, by the bylaws or by an agreement among any number of security holders.
claims.quote: may be imposed by the certificate of incorporation or by the bylaws or by an agreement among any number of security holders

claims.sentence: A restriction may be imposed by an agreement among such holders and the corporation.
claims.quote: or among such holders and the corporation

claims.sentence: It says a restriction is permitted if, among other things, it obliges the holder to offer the securities to the corporation, or to others, first.
claims.quote: Obligates the holder of the restricted securities to offer to the corporation

claims.sentence: It says a restriction is permitted if, among other things, it obliges the corporation or a holder to purchase them.
claims.quote: Obligates the corporation or any holder of securities of the corporation or any other person or any combination of the foregoing, to purchase

claims.sentence: It also provides that a restriction must be noted conspicuously on the certificate, or contained in the notice given for uncertificated shares.
claims.quote: noted conspicuously on the certificate or certificates representing the security or securities so restricted

claims.sentence: It also provides that otherwise a restriction is ineffective except against a person with actual knowledge of it.
claims.quote: is ineffective except against a person with actual knowledge of the restriction

claims.sentence: The IRS says that if you receive stock for services and the stock is nontransferable or subject to a substantial risk of forfeiture, you generally do not include its value in income until it becomes substantially vested.
claims.quote: nontransferable or subject to a substantial risk of forfeiture, you don't include the value of the property in your income until it becomes substantially vested

claims.sentence: It also describes an election to include the value in income in the year of transfer instead.
claims.quote: You can choose to include the value of the property in your income in the year it's transferred to you

claims.sentence: The default rule in subsection (a) is that the value of such property is included in the gross income of the person who performed the services.
claims.quote: shall be included in the gross income of the person who performed such services

claims.sentence: The default rule is that the value is included in the first taxable year in which that person's rights in the property are transferable or are not subject to a substantial risk of forfeiture, whichever applies.
claims.quote: are transferable or are not subject to a substantial risk of forfeiture, whichever is applicable

claims.sentence: Subsection (b) says any person who performs services in connection with which property is transferred may elect to include in gross income for the taxable year in which the property is transferred the excess, if any, of the fair market value of the property at the time of transfer over the amount paid for it.
claims.quote: may elect to include in his gross income for the taxable year in which such property is transferred

claims.sentence: The statute says the value is determined without regard to any restriction other than one which by its terms will never lapse.
claims.quote: determined without regard to any restriction other than a restriction which by its terms will never lapse

claims.sentence: In the IRS's words in Publication 525, a person who makes the choice finds that the substantial vesting rules do not apply.
claims.locator: Publication 525, Choosing to include in income for year of transfer
claims.quote: If you make this choice, the substantial vesting rules don't apply

claims.sentence: In the IRS's words in Publication 525, generally any later appreciation in value is not included in compensation when the property becomes substantially vested.
claims.locator: Publication 525, Choosing to include in income for year of transfer
claims.quote: generally, any later appreciation in value isn't included in your compensation when the property becomes substantially vested

claims.sentence: The regulation adds that paying full value for the property, realizing no bargain element, does not preclude use of the election.
claims.quote: the transferee has paid full value for the property transferred, realizing no bargain element in the transaction, does not preclude the use of the election

claims.sentence: The statute at section 83(b)(2) gives a period: the election is filed not later than 30 days after the date the property was transferred.
claims.quote: shall be made not later than 30 days after the date of such transfer

claims.sentence: The regulation at 26 CFR 1.83-2(b) gives the same period.
claims.quote: shall be filed not later than 30 days after the date the property was transferred

claims.sentence: The regulation adds that it may be filed before the date of transfer.
claims.quote: may be filed prior to the date of transfer

claims.sentence: The Form 15620 instructions give the same period.
claims.quote: must be filed no later than 30 days after the date the property was transferred

claims.sentence: Publication 525 gives the same period.
claims.locator: Publication 525, How to make the choice
claims.quote: You must file this statement no later than 30 days after the date the property was transferred

claims.sentence: They say that, under section 7503 of the Code, if the thirtieth day following the transfer falls on a Saturday, Sunday or legal holiday.
claims.quote: if the thirtieth day following the transfer of property falls on a Saturday, Sunday or legal holiday

claims.sentence: The election is considered timely filed if it is postmarked by the next succeeding day that is not a Saturday, Sunday or legal holiday.
claims.quote: the election will be considered timely filed if it is postmarked by the next succeeding day which is not a Saturday, Sunday or legal holiday

claims.sentence: What counts as the date of transfer for a given grant is a question for a tax professional; the form's instructions point to the regulation on transfers.
claims.quote: For more information on what constitutes a transfer of property for purposes of IRC § 83, see Treas. Reg. § 1.83-3(a)

claims.sentence: The regulation says the election is made by filing one copy of a written statement with the internal revenue office with which the person who performed the services files their return.
claims.quote: made by filing one copy of a written statement with the internal revenue office with which the person who performed the services files his return

claims.sentence: Publication 525 and the form's own instructions both say the choice can be made by filing a written statement or Form 15620.
claims.locator: Publication 525, How to make the choice
claims.quote: You can make the choice by filing a written statement or Form 15620

claims.sentence: The instructions say that in the alternative an election may be made by a written statement that satisfies the requirements of the regulation.
claims.quote: an 83(b) election may be made by filing a written statement that satisfies the requirements of Treas. Reg. § 1.83-2

claims.sentence: The regulation lists what the statement must contain: the name, address and taxpayer identification number of the taxpayer.
claims.quote: The name, address and taxpayer identification number of the taxpayer

claims.sentence: The regulation lists what the statement must contain: a description of each property for which the election is made.
claims.quote: A description of each property

claims.sentence: The regulation lists what the statement must contain: the nature of the restriction or restrictions to which the property is subject.
claims.quote: The nature of the restriction or restrictions to which the property is subject

claims.sentence: The regulation lists what the statement must contain: the fair market value at the time of transfer, determined without regard to any lapse restriction, of each property.
claims.quote: determined without regard to any lapse restriction

claims.sentence: The regulation lists what the statement must contain: the amount, if any, paid for the property.
claims.quote: The amount (if any) paid for such property

claims.sentence: It also requires that the statement be signed by the person making the election and that it say it is being made under section 83(b).
claims.quote: signed by the person making the election

claims.sentence: Form 15620 collects the same information in numbered boxes.
claims.quote: Enter the name, TIN, and address of the person making the 83(b) election

claims.sentence: The form's instructions say to submit the completed and signed form by mail to the IRS office with which the person who performs the services files a federal income tax return.
claims.quote: to the IRS via mail with the IRS office with which the person who performs the services files a federal income tax return

claims.sentence: The regulation says the person who performed the services also submits a copy to the person for whom the services are performed.
claims.quote: shall also submit a copy of the statement referred to in paragraph (c) of this section to the person for whom the services are performed

claims.sentence: The instructions say the person who performs the services is also required to submit a copy to the person for whom the services are performed.
claims.quote: also required to submit a copy of the completed and signed Form 15620 to the person for whom the services are performed

claims.sentence: The statute says the election may not be revoked except with the consent of the Secretary.
claims.quote: Such election may not be revoked except with the consent of the Secretary

claims.sentence: The regulation says consent will be granted only where the transferee is under a mistake of fact as to the underlying transaction.
claims.quote: Consent will be granted only in the case where the transferee is under a mistake of fact as to the underlying transaction

claims.sentence: The regulation says consent must be requested within 60 days of the date the mistake first became known.
claims.quote: must be requested within 60 days of the date on which the mistake of fact first became known

claims.sentence: It adds that a mistake as to value, or a decline in value, of the property, or a failure to perform an act contemplated at the time of transfer, does not constitute a mistake of fact.
claims.quote: does not constitute a mistake of fact

claims.sentence: The Form 15620 instructions refer readers to that regulation and to Revenue Procedure 2006-31.
claims.quote: refer to Treas. Reg. § 1.83–2(f) and Revenue Procedure 2006-31

claims.sentence: The statute says that if the property is subsequently forfeited, no deduction is allowed in respect of the forfeiture.
claims.quote: no deduction shall be allowed in respect of such forfeiture

claims.sentence: Publication 525 describes the loss on forfeiture as the amount paid for the property minus the amount realized on the forfeiture.
claims.locator: Publication 525, Choosing to include in income for year of transfer
claims.quote: your loss is the amount you paid for the property minus any amount you realized on the forfeiture

claims.sentence: The regulation says the loss is a capital loss if the property is a capital asset.
claims.quote: If such property is a capital asset in the hands of the taxpayer, such loss shall be a capital loss

claims.sentence: Publication 525 says you can't make this choice for a statutory or nonstatutory stock option.
claims.locator: Publication 525, Choosing to include in income for year of transfer
claims.quote: You can't make this choice for a statutory or nonstatutory stock option

claims.sentence: The Open Source Initiative's definition begins by saying that open source does not just mean access to the source code, and that the distribution terms must meet a list of criteria.
claims.quote: Open source doesn't just mean access to the source code

claims.sentence: The first says the license shall not restrict any party from selling or giving away the software as a component of an aggregate software distribution containing programs from several different sources.
claims.quote: shall not restrict any party from selling or giving away the software as a component of an aggregate software distribution

claims.sentence: The first says the license shall not require a royalty or other fee for such sale.
claims.quote: shall not require a royalty or other fee for such sale

claims.sentence: Another says the license must not restrict anyone from making use of the program in a specific field of endeavor, and gives as an example that it may not restrict the program from being used in a business.
claims.quote: may not restrict the program from being used in a business

claims.sentence: The MIT text grants permission, free of charge, to deal in the software without restriction, including the rights to use, copy, modify, merge, publish, distribute, sublicense and sell copies.
claims.quote: to use, copy, modify, merge, publish, distribute, sublicense, and/or sell copies of the Software

claims.sentence: It makes one condition: the copyright notice and the permission notice shall be included in all copies or substantial portions of the software.
claims.quote: shall be included in all copies or substantial portions of the Software

claims.sentence: It then says the software is provided as is, without warranty.
claims.quote: THE SOFTWARE IS PROVIDED "AS IS", WITHOUT WARRANTY OF ANY KIND

claims.sentence: Apache 2.0 grants a copyright license, which the table summarizes as a copyright license.
claims.quote: each Contributor hereby grants to You a perpetual, worldwide, non-exclusive, no-charge, royalty-free, irrevocable copyright license

claims.sentence: Section 3 grants each contributor's patent license, limited to patent claims necessarily infringed by their contribution, alone or combined with the work.
claims.quote: necessarily infringed by their Contribution(s) alone or by combination of their Contribution(s) with the Work

claims.sentence: It also says that if you institute patent litigation alleging that the work constitutes direct or contributory patent infringement, any patent licenses granted to you under the license for that work terminate as of the date the litigation is filed.
claims.quote: shall terminate as of the date such litigation is filed

claims.sentence: Section 4 sets the redistribution conditions: give recipients a copy of the license.
claims.quote: You must give any other recipients of the Work or Derivative Works a copy of this License

claims.sentence: Section 4 sets the redistribution conditions: cause modified files to carry prominent notices that you changed them.
claims.quote: You must cause any modified files to carry prominent notices stating that You changed the files

claims.sentence: Section 4 sets the redistribution conditions: retain copyright, patent, trademark and attribution notices in the source form of derivative works.
claims.quote: all copyright, patent, trademark, and attribution notices

claims.sentence: If the work includes a NOTICE text file, include a readable copy of its attribution notices in one of the places the section lists.
claims.quote: must include a readable copy of the attribution notices

claims.sentence: To propagate means to do anything that, without permission, would make you liable for infringement under copyright law, except executing a work on a computer or modifying a private copy.
claims.quote: except executing it on a computer or modifying a private copy

claims.sentence: To convey means any kind of propagation that enables other parties to make or receive copies.
claims.quote: any kind of propagation that enables other parties to make or receive copies

claims.sentence: The text adds that mere interaction with a user through a computer network, with no transfer of a copy, is not conveying.
claims.quote: Mere interaction with a user through a computer network, with no transfer of a copy, is not conveying

claims.sentence: Section 2 grants unlimited permission to run the unmodified program.
claims.quote: unlimited permission to run the unmodified Program

claims.sentence: Section 2 says you may make, run and propagate covered works that you do not convey, without conditions, so long as your license remains in force.
claims.quote: You may make, run and propagate covered works that you do not convey, without conditions so long as your license otherwise remains in force

claims.sentence: Section 5 says that when you convey a work based on the program, you must license the entire work, as a whole, under the GPL to anyone who comes into possession of a copy.
claims.quote: You must license the entire work, as a whole, under this License to anyone who comes into possession of a copy

claims.sentence: Section 6 says that when you convey object code, you must also convey the machine-readable Corresponding Source in one of the ways the section lists.
claims.quote: you also convey the machine-readable Corresponding Source under the terms of this License

claims.sentence: Corresponding Source is defined as all the source needed to generate, install, run and modify the object code.
claims.quote: all the source code needed to generate, install, and (for an executable work) run the object code and to modify the work

claims.sentence: The definition says it includes the source code for shared libraries and dynamically linked subprograms that the work is specifically designed to require, for example by intimate data communication or control flow.
claims.quote: shared libraries and dynamically linked subprograms that the work is specifically designed to require, such as by intimate data communication or control flow

claims.sentence: The text also distinguishes an aggregate, a compilation of a covered work with other separate and independent works that are not combined with it so as to form a larger program.
claims.quote: which are not combined with it such as to form a larger program

claims.sentence: It says inclusion of a covered work in an aggregate does not cause the license to apply to the other parts.
claims.quote: Inclusion of a covered work in an aggregate does not cause this License to apply to the other parts of the aggregate

claims.sentence: Section 8 covers termination: an attempt to propagate or modify a covered work other than as the license permits is void and automatically terminates your rights.
claims.quote: is void, and will automatically terminate your rights under this License

claims.sentence: Its section 13 then adds one clause that applies notwithstanding any other provision of this License.
claims.quote: Notwithstanding any other provision of this License

claims.sentence: If you modify the program, your modified version must prominently offer all users interacting with it remotely through a computer network an opportunity to receive the Corresponding Source of your version, from a network server at no charge.
claims.quote: your modified version must prominently offer all users interacting with it remotely through a computer network

claims.sentence: The AGPL text carries the same statement that mere interaction through a network is not conveying.
claims.quote: Mere interaction with a user through a computer network, with no transfer of a copy, is not conveying

claims.sentence: Apache 2.0 section 5 says a contribution intentionally submitted to the licensor is under the license.
claims.quote: any Contribution intentionally submitted for inclusion in the Work by You to the Licensor shall be under the terms and conditions of this License

claims.sentence: Apache 2.0 section 5 says a contribution intentionally submitted to the licensor is under the license unless you state otherwise.
claims.quote: Unless You explicitly state otherwise

claims.sentence: The SPDX License List gives each commonly found license a standardized short identifier, a full name, the license text and a canonical permanent URL.
claims.quote: includes a standardized short identifier, the full name, the license text, and a canonical permanent URL for each license and exception

claims.sentence: The purpose is that licenses can be identified reliably in an SPDX document, in source files or elsewhere.
claims.quote: enable efficient and reliable identification of such licenses and exceptions in an SPDX document, in source files or elsewhere

claims.sentence: The OSI page for the MIT License, for example, shows its SPDX short identifier as MIT.
claims.quote: SPDX short identifier: MIT

claims.sentence: The GDPR defines personal data as any information relating to an identified or identifiable natural person.
claims.quote: any information relating to an identified or identifiable natural person ('data subject')

claims.sentence: An identifiable person is one who can be identified, directly or indirectly, by reference to an identifier such as a name, an identification number, location data or an online identifier.
claims.quote: can be identified, directly or indirectly, in particular by reference to an identifier such as a name, an identification number, location data

claims.sentence: The definition of personal data names an online identifier.
claims.quote: location data, an online identifier or to one or more factors

claims.sentence: It defines processing as any operation or set of operations performed on personal data.
claims.quote: 'processing' means any operation or set of operations which is performed on personal data

claims.sentence: Processing includes operations such as collection, storage, use, disclosure, and erasure.
claims.quote: such as collection, recording, organisation, structuring, storage, adaptation or alteration, retrieval, consultation, use, disclosure by transmission

claims.sentence: Article 3 says the GDPR applies to processing in the context of the activities of an establishment of a controller or processor in the Union.
claims.quote: applies to the processing of personal data in the context of the activities of an establishment of a controller or a processor in the Union

claims.sentence: For a controller or processor not established in the Union, it applies to processing of data subjects in the Union related to offering goods or services, irrespective of whether payment is required.
claims.quote: the offering of goods or services, irrespective of whether a payment of the data subject is required, to such data subjects in the Union

claims.sentence: Or to monitoring their behaviour as far as it takes place within the Union.
claims.quote: the monitoring of their behaviour as far as their behaviour takes place within the Union

claims.sentence: Article 6(1) says processing is lawful only if at least one of six conditions applies.
claims.quote: Processing shall be lawful only if and to the extent that at least one of the following applies

claims.sentence: The conditions include the data subject's consent to one or more specific purposes.
claims.quote: the data subject has given consent to the processing of his or her personal data for one or more specific purposes

claims.sentence: They include necessity for the performance of a contract with the data subject.
claims.quote: processing is necessary for the performance of a contract to which the data subject is party

claims.sentence: They include compliance with a legal obligation.
claims.quote: processing is necessary for compliance with a legal obligation to which the controller is subject

claims.sentence: They include the legitimate interests pursued by the controller, except where overridden by the interests or rights of the data subject.

claims.sentence: It lists as material connections a business, family or personal relationship.
claims.quote: Material connections can include a business, family, or personal relationship.

claims.sentence: It lists monetary payment and free or discounted products as material connections.
claims.quote: They can include monetary payment or the provision of free or discounted products

claims.sentence: It lists benefits such as early access to a product or the possibility of being paid.
claims.quote: other benefits to the endorser, such as early access to a product or the possibility of being paid

claims.sentence: Section 465.1 defines a consumer review as a consumer's, or purported consumer's, evaluation of a product, service or business.
claims.quote: a consumer's evaluation, or a purported consumer's evaluation, of a product, service, or business that is submitted by the consumer or purported consumer

claims.sentence: The evaluation is published to a website or platform dedicated in whole or in part to receiving and displaying such evaluations.
claims.quote: published to a website or platform dedicated in whole or in part to receiving and displaying such evaluations

claims.sentence: Consumer reviews include ratings whether or not they have text.
claims.quote: consumer reviews include consumer ratings regardless of whether they include any text or narrative

claims.sentence: The rule defines related promotional messages as well.
claims.quote: means an advertising or promotional message (including verbal statements, demonstrations, or depictions of the name, signature, likeness

claims.sentence: The FTC's rule at 16 CFR part 465 addresses fake and false reviews.
claims.quote: Fake or false consumer reviews

claims.sentence: Section 465.2 says it is an unfair or deceptive act or practice for a business to write, create or sell a consumer review that materially misrepresents the reviewer's existence, use of the product or experience.
claims.quote: an unfair or deceptive act or practice and a violation of this part for a business to write, create, or sell a consumer review

claims.sentence: The misrepresentation is that the reviewer exists, that the reviewer used the product, or the reviewer's experience.
claims.quote: That the reviewer exists; (2) That the reviewer used or otherwise had experience with the product, service, or business

claims.sentence: It reaches a business that buys such a review.
claims.quote: for a business to purchase a consumer review

claims.sentence: It applies when the business knew or should have known the review was misleading.
claims.quote: which the business knew or should have known materially misrepresented

claims.sentence: It reaches a business that procures a review from its officers, managers, employees or agents, or their immediate relatives, for posting on a third-party platform.
claims.quote: procure a consumer review from its officers, managers, employees, or agents, or any of their immediate relatives, for posting on a third-party platform or website

claims.sentence: Paragraph (d) of section 465.2 says the provisions on bought and procured reviews do not apply to reviews that resulted from generalized solicitations to purchasers to post their experiences.
claims.quote: a business making generalized solicitations to purchasers to post reviews

claims.sentence: Paragraph (d) also excludes a business merely hosting reviews.
claims.quote: Reviews that appear on a website or platform as a result of the business merely engaging in consumer review hosting

sentences.sentence: The documents a company signs in its first year include the entity filing, the equity split, the assignment of code and the legal pages on the product.
The articles on this desk describe what each one is for and what the public sources say about it, so that a founder can bring specific questions to their own lawyer.
The eight articles run from the company outward.

They cover choosing an entity, founder equity and vesting, the 83(b) election and its deadline, founder IP assignment and confidentiality, open-source licenses, privacy law, the terms of service and privacy policy, and trademark name clearance.
World Enterprise is not a law firm, and nothing on this desk is legal or tax advice.
Each article carries a dated general-information line, reads primary sources such as statutes and agency pages, and ends with what it cannot tell you.

The pieces cover what diligence tests, the records small engineering teams keep in order, questions for your own counsel, the founder time a raise consumes, investor fit, and how to arrange an evidence pack, answer a security and privacy questionnaire and keep customer evidence.
